claims.text: The starting material consists of sub-5 nm AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles produced by pulsed laser deposition on a silicon nitride membrane.
The as-grown AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles initially have an FCC structure.
The PLD-grown nanoparticles may contain kinetically trapped, non-equilibrium elemental distributions.
High configurational entropy and sluggish diffusion are expected to stabilize an FCC solid solution against segregation and coalescence.
In sub-5 nm AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles, surface-energy minimization overrides nominally sluggish bulk diffusion.
Surface-energy gradients create chemical-potential differences between the nanoparticle core and surface.
Au and Cu have sufficiently low surface or cohesive energies to preferentially migrate to the nanoparticle surface.
Surface-mediated migration of Au and Cu can bypass the barrier associated with sluggish bulk diffusion.
For particles below 10 nm, the surface free-energy contribution, gamma times area, dominates the configurational-entropy contribution.
The resulting chemical-potential gradient accelerates Au and Cu surface diffusion and produces surface enrichment.
Surface-enriched Au and Cu evaporate because their vapor pressures are high relative to refractory components such as Pt.
Au and Cu evaporation causes nanoparticle shrinkage, loss of sub-5 nm particles, and widening of the size distribution.
The surface-segregation and evaporation mechanism is expected to become dominant at approximately 600-800 K.
Above the critical temperature, Au and Cu surface segregation and evaporation become faster than bulk diffusion.
Above the critical temperature, the population shifts toward larger segregated cores or the smallest particles disappear completely.
Icosahedral nanoparticles have higher initial surface energy and defect density than truncated-octahedral nanoparticles.
Icosahedral particles will degrade faster than truncated octahedra because of their higher initial surface energy.
The proposed mechanism is restricted to nanoparticles smaller than 10 nm.
For bulk material or particles larger than 20 nm, bulk entropy and sluggish diffusion remain the dominant stabilizing effects.
Variation in the initial kinetic trapping of PLD-grown particles can change the onset temperature of segregation.

contradictions.description: The design says the simulations allow surface-energy minimization while enforcing high diffusion barriers, whereas the measurements call for comparison with simulations in which surface diffusion is artificially suppressed. It is unclear how surface-energy-driven segregation can occur in the nominal test model if the diffusion pathway needed to realize it is suppressed.
